text: The Sea Organization (Sea Org) is the highest-ranking group within the Church of Scientology’s network of corporations, though it is not incorporated. Established on August 12, 1967, by L. Ron Hubbard aboard three ships—the Avon River, the Enchanter, and HMS Royal Scotsman, later renamed the Diana, the Athena, and the Apollo—the Sea Org began as Hubbard’s private navy and adopted naval uniforms and ranks. The Apollo served as the flagship, with Hubbard referred to as Commodore. In 1975, the organization moved to land-based operations, though maritime customs persist, including naval-style uniforms and the use of "sir" for addressing officers. The Sea Org maintains strict codes, requiring members to sign a symbolic billion-year pledge of service, which is not legally binding but represents a lifelong commitment to Scientology. Members receive free room and board, a weekly allowance of about $50, and are expected to work at least 100 hours per week, live in communal housing called berthing, and adhere to rules such as disavowing premarital sex and prohibiting extramarital relationships. Members may marry within the organization but must leave if they have or wish to raise children. The Sea Org’s mission, described as "an exploration into both time and space," includes administering church policies and managing key organizations. David Miscavige, the current leader, holds the rank of captain, while the rank of commodore is permanently reserved for the reincarnation of L. Ron Hubbard. The organization’s structure and practices have been described by scholars and ex-members as totalitarian, involving intensive surveillance, lack of freedom, and strict discipline. In 1971, the Sea Org took over the delivery of upper-level auditing (Operating Thetan or OT) levels, and in 1981, under Miscavige’s Commodore’s Messenger Organization, it dissolved the Guardian’s Office and later reassigned its duties to the Office of Special Affairs. In 1987, the church purchased the Freewinds, a 440-foot motor vessel, which docks in Curaçao and serves as a religious retreat and training center, hosting OT VIII—the highest auditing level—and events like the annual Maiden Voyage. All new recruits must complete a compulsory novitiate known as the Estates Project Force (EPF), a boot camp-style program where recruits are not considered full members, must run instead of walk, are separated from spouses, and undergo five hours of manual labor and five hours of study called "Product Zero." They graduate upon completing required courses, passing a mandatory "7A Security Check," and receiving approval from a "Fitness Board." Members formally reaffirm their 18-point pledge annually on Sea Org Day, August 12, the organization’s founding anniversary. The Sea Org’s motto is "Revenimus" ("We Come Back"), reflecting the belief that members will return to the organization upon rebirth. Former members have reported harsh conditions, including in the Rehabilitation Project Force (RPF), established in 1974, which involves isolation, rigid schedules, grueling labor, and psychological control, with some members spending years in the program. Scholars and former members have compared the Sea Org to a paramilitary group, noting its use of military-style discipline, training in works like The Art of War and On War, and the existence of an elite unit called the "SEALs." The organization has faced criticism for practices including forced child labor, coerced abortions, human trafficking, mental abuse, and sexual assaults. In 2000, the Sea Org had approximately 5,800 members, primarily residing in Los Angeles, Clearwater, Copenhagen, London, Saint Hill, and Sydney, with some in smaller centers. According to a 2022 report by the Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission, the UK arm of Scientology reported 700 "volunteers" (including Sea Org members) across several locations. Members who leave are issued a "freeloader's bill" for auditing and training received, which is not legally enforceable but prevents them from accessing services until paid and completing an amends program. The Sea Org was founded as a way to escape government scrutiny, including from the FDA, IRS, and other national governments, by operating on the high seas. According to Hubbard, the Sea Org is modeled after the "Loyal Officers" who overthrew the tyrant Xenu in the Galactic Confederacy, and is an idealized version of his World War II military experience, reminiscent of the "Soldiers of Light" in his science fiction works. The publicized goal is to "get ethics in on the planet." In 1975, the church sold its ships and transitioned to land-based operations, with centers in Clearwater, Copenhagen, London, Los Angeles, Mexico City, Saint Hill, Sydney, and other global locations. High Winds is the Sea Org’s official magazine, first published on Sea Org Day 1980. The Sea Org Day ceremonies include rank promotions and commemorations of members’ contributions. Sea Org members are required to sign a symbolic billion-year commitment, pledging to "get ethics in on this planet and the universe," and are expected to return upon rebirth. Children of Sea Org members are often placed in the Cadet Org until age six, after which they are raised communally and allowed limited visits to parents. Several former members have reported being advised or forced to have abortions to avoid lower organizational placements. Scientology opposes abortion and actively promotes it in its publications. The Sea Org is described as a spiritual commitment that is beyond the full understanding of non-Scientologists, and the Church of Scientology International has stated that the Sea Org has no secular or ecclesiastical organizational structure, only a colloquial usage implying its existence. All policy and administrative roles in key church organizations are held by Sea Org members.
